name: Oral surgeon

pf.license.need: each oral surgeon holds their own license from the state's dental board; a surgical assistant holds one only where the state licenses assistants
pf.license.who: each person; the practice too where the state's form registers dental or surgical offices or their owners
pf.license.ask: each person's license number in their invite reply, or the owner sends it; the practice's registration and any mobile permit number come from the owner. The owner may leave a number out
pf.license.check: Rosie does not look up, check or verify a license number. The owner gives it, and it is shown where the state asks
pf.license.blocks: no booking is held or refused because of a license: the owner states it, and that is the record
pf.license.away: visits at a care home, a school or a home only where the state's rules allow mobile or portable dental surgery; a mobile or portable dental permit where the state's form asks for one (a switch)
pf.license.sedation: no sedation or general anesthesia is booked by Rosie. The office plans any sedation itself, with the patient, by phone; Rosie never prices, confirms or moves it
pf.license.agreement: a health privacy agreement (a HIPAA business associate agreement) signed on the secure page before the first booking; every company in Rosie's chain signs one with Rosie
pf.license.renewals: if the owner records an expiry date, Rosie reminds the owner 30 days before it; Rosie does not check the license
pf.license.insurance: malpractice insurance where the state's form asks for it; the owner states it, and Rosie does not check it

pf.services.shape: visit types in a surgical chair, each with a set length; a tooth removal is a surgery visit with a set length and a recovery check after it; a post-surgery problem is booked the same day with the owner's OK; every visit needs a free chair
pf.services.examples: the example offices' own prices (Lee Oral Surgery and Lee Home Surgery), not a standard; a plan pays its own share for surgery, up to its yearly limit, and the patient's share is an estimate

list.name: New patient consult (X-rays and a scan, then the surgeon's exam)
list.kind: one price; the plan's estimate is shown when a plan pays
list.length: 60 min: 30 with the assistant (X-rays and scan), then 30 with the surgeon
list.after: the patient's share at the front desk
list.note: new-patient times are kept apart (Sam's booking rules)

list.name: Tooth removal (simple, with local numbing only)
list.price: $140 (the example office's price; a second tooth at the same visit is added)
list.length: 45 min, with a recovery check after
list.after: the $100 rest at the chair, after the removal
list.note: no sedation here: sedation is planned by phone and is never booked by Rosie

list.name: Stitch removal and check
list.kind: one price, paid in full when booked

list.name: Night guard or surgical splint, made from photos
list.length: 2 visits: the photos, then the fitting
list.before: a $20 deposit once the surgeon's quote is OK'd
list.after: the rest ($70) at the front desk, at the fitting
list.note: the surgeon OKs the quote before any deposit

list.name: Post-surgery problem (swelling, a dry socket, a sore spot)
list.price: the $25 check is promised; any treatment is priced at the chair (the example: $110 in all)
list.note: the owner OKs same-day times first

list.name: Second tooth removed at the same visit
list.note: only when the surgeon plans it with the patient's yes

list.name: Surgery check at a care home
list.kind: one price; the plan's share when a plan pays
list.where: at the customer's place (a care home or a home)
list.before: nothing taken when a plan pays; private pay gets Rosfield's bill after the visit
list.after: the office bills the plan its own way; private pay: Rosie texts the bill

list.name: Broken tooth or a loose stitch at a care home
list.price: the $89 visit fee is promised; any repair is priced at the visit (the example: $245 in all)

list.name: Multi-tooth extraction plan at a care home, quoted from photos and X-rays
list.length: 2 visits: the plan, then the removal under local numbing only
list.before: a $160 deposit when the plan is OK'd (25%)
list.after: Rosie texts the bill for the $480 rest when the surgeon texts DONE

list.name: School oral health screening day
list.price: set with the school: free to families, or billed to each child's plan
list.length: a whole morning, one portable kit
list.after: the office bills plans its own way
list.note: each child needs a parent's or guardian's signed consent on the secure page

pf.services.capacity: one patient per chair; the office's chairs and the portable kit are booked like people
pf.services.nobodyHome: never: the patient is always there
pf.services.online: none: a removal or a stitch check needs the chair; a question by video is answered by the office, not booked as a visit

beforeTimes: for you, your child, or someone you help (a care home resident)
which visit: the office's own visit types only (a new patient consult, a tooth removal, a stitch check, a night guard, or a post-surgery problem), never a symptom typed into the AI
a dental or medical plan (its name only) or paying yourself
afterTime: anything the office should know to help, like a wheelchair or needing an interpreter
for a care home visit: the place's name, the room, and who meets the surgeon
securePage: plan member ID, the plan holder and a photo of the plan card
health history: medicines, blood thinners, allergies, conditions, and past surgery
a parent's or guardian's consent for anyone under 18, or the consent of the person who decides for an adult who can't
pf.questions.whoMayBook: an adult for themselves; a parent or guardian for anyone under 18; a guardian or health care agent for an adult who can't consent; the care home's staff for a resident, with the decider's consent on the secure page; a minor alone only where the state's rules let minors consent to dental surgery (a switch)
pf.questions.neverAsked: symptoms, reasons or results are never asked or typed in the AI chat

stop.words: face or jaw swelling with a fever, or trouble breathing or swallowing
stop.say: This needs care now. Go to the nearest emergency room or call 911. Don't wait for a surgery visit.
stop.booking: no booking; the same words are repeated if a same-day request is declined

stop.words: bleeding after a tooth removal that won't stop, or a tooth knocked out
stop.say: Bite hard on clean gauze or a damp tea bag for 20 minutes. If it won't stop, go to the emergency room or call 911. For a knocked-out tooth, call the office's own line now.
stop.booking: no booking by the AI; the office's own line

stop.words: swallowed something poisonous, or too much of a medicine
stop.say: Call Poison Help now at 1-800-222-1222, or 911 if they're not awake or not breathing.

goOn.words: a sore or swollen spot after a removal, with nothing else
goOn.what: matched to the office's own post-surgery visit; Rosie never judges how urgent it is

pf.safety.always: the general screen: danger to life, fire, gas or a medical emergency gets 911, and words about self-harm get 988

steps.name: Health history, consent and the plan's papers
steps.when: on the secure page only, never by text; due the day before the visit (a same-day visit: before the time is held); one reminder before it's due
steps.who: every new patient; returning patients once a year, or when their health changes
steps.result: not done by its due date: Sam keeps the visit (signed on the secure page at the desk or the door, before any work), moves it, or cancels with no fee

steps.name: The plan check
steps.when: while booking, by the front desk, by hand
steps.who: every patient who names a plan
steps.result: covered, some services only, not covered, or can't check now (the desk checks later, and the patient may cancel free)

steps.name: A written price estimate for self-pay patients
steps.when: told while booking; sent within 1 business day (the example office's rule), or sooner where the rules require it
steps.result: a to-do for the front desk, with its due date

steps.name: A signed surgical consent
steps.when: on the secure page, before the surgery visit, with the price and the deposit shown first
steps.who: every surgery patient, and the parent or guardian for a child
steps.result: not signed by the surgery visit: the visit waits; Sam moves it or cancels with no fee

steps.name: The care home's OK
steps.who: the host place agrees to host the visits
steps.result: no OK: no times at that place

pf.first_steps.prep: eat and drink as the surgeon's sheet says; arrive 15 minutes early; bring a photo ID, the plan card and the medicine list; a surgery visit needs an adult to take you home; at a care home: the resident's medicine list ready with the nurse

pf.visit.checkIn: at the office: the check-in code at the front desk; at a care home or school: the code from the patient, or from the nurse or staff member named on the booking
pf.visit.beforeWork: the assistant takes the X-rays and reads the health history first; the surgeon checks for changes before any work
pf.visit.changes: an extra tooth or a second step is priced and OK'd before it's done; the plan's estimate is shown first; a new step is booked as its own visit only with the patient's yes
pf.visit.done: the check-in code or DONE; the surgeon's notes, X-rays and scans stay in the office's own records, never in Rosie or a text
pf.visit.away: a portable kit (a light, a chair, suction and gauze); the care home's nurse is told when the visit is done

pf.money.before: nothing taken at booking for a consult or a stitch check (the office bills dental and medical plans); a card saved only where the office turns on its missed-visit fee; a tooth removal: a $40 deposit when booked, and the rest at the chair; a night guard from photos: a $20 deposit once the quote is OK'd; at a care home: nothing taken when a plan pays, a $160 deposit when a multi-tooth plan is OK'd, the rest on Rosfield's bill
pf.money.plans: the plans the office takes (its own list); the front desk checks each plan by hand and records it: active or not, what it pays for surgery and up to what yearly limit; the patient's share is an estimate, not a promise
pf.money.selfPay: a self-pay patient is told while booking that they can get a written price estimate, and gets it on time; a bill far above it can be disputed (the federal rules set how)
pf.money.fees: the missed-visit fee: $20 at the example office, only when the owner turns it on; a card is saved for it, and the same fee applies to every patient who may be charged one
pf.money.feeFree: a switch: no fee ever for patients whose plan or the state's rules bar one (like Medicaid, where that applies), or whom the owner marks fee-free; their texts say 'No fee to cancel or miss'
pf.money.after: claims sent by the office; the patient pays their share at the front desk, its own way; a balance after the plan pays is billed by the office, not by Rosie's text; at a care home, the office bills its own way, and private pay gets the bill Rosie texts
pf.money.rosfield: the business pays Rosfield's $2 per confirmed booking, as every business does (the $2 is counted when the visit's check-in code is entered; no visit, no $2); card payments also cost Stripe's own card fee
pf.money.caps: deposit cap: from the state form; fee limits for plan patients: from the plan's and the state's rules

pf.messages.never: texts carry only the practice's name, the date, the time, the address and a secure link: never the visit type, the plan, the reason, the results, the medicines or the surgeon's name (when the surgeon comes to a care home or home, the name stays, for the door check); X-rays and scans never go through Rosie
pf.messages.staff: texts to the owner and staff use the patient's initials only (A.M., never Alex M.)
pf.messages.minors: a minor's texts go to the parent or guardian; a minor who may consent alone gets texts only on their own phone, with no visit type
pf.messages.decider: for an adult who can't consent, the texts go to the person who decides, and the code to whoever meets the surgeon

pf.staff.licenses: each oral surgeon's own license, per state; a surgical assistant's own license only where the state licenses assistants
pf.staff.skills: oral surgeons: extractions, surgical consults, night guards and post-surgery care; surgical assistants: X-rays, scans, chair setup, recovery checks and the work the state allows; only people cleared for mobile visits go to care homes and homes
pf.staff.supervision: an assistant works only while the surgeon is in the office or on the portable visit, as the state's rules allow (a switch: some states let assistants work alone at schools and care homes)
pf.staff.oks: the owner OKs same-day post-surgery times, quotes over $500, and anything an assistant flags
pf.staff.standIn: an assistant out: the surgeon does the recovery check, or new times; the surgeon out: another oral surgeon takes the visit, or new times with no fee
pf.staff.away: the team at a care home or school is the people cleared for mobile visits, with the portable kit; sedation is never given at a care home or a home

pf.rules.records: surgical records are kept by the office for as long as the state's rules require (a child's records may be kept longer); a delete request removes only Rosie's own booking details, never the office's records
pf.rules.copies: a patient's copy of their records within the time the rules set; Rosie sends only booking and payment records
pf.rules.showLicense: the license shown where the state asks: posted at the office, and on a visit away from it
pf.rules.minors: who may consent for a minor, and at what age a minor may consent alone (a switch from the state form)
pf.rules.host: a visit at a care home or school only under the host's written OK, and the host's sign-in rules; visit days at a host's place (S1-58) need the host's standing OK on file; the example's care home visits are booked one resident at a time under the care home's OK, so no visit days are set
pf.rules.ads: no free-consult or price claims the state's rules don't allow
pf.rules.privacy: health privacy rules for every message and form

pf.edges.lateArrival: more than 15 minutes late: still seen, but a surgery may move to another day (the office decides; Rosie never changes the booking itself)
pf.edges.standIn: a surgeon or assistant out: a stand-in who may do that part, or new times with no fee
pf.edges.forms: a form not done by its due date: one reminder, then Sam keeps the visit (signed on the secure page before any work), moves it, or cancels with no fee (A7-74, B7-61)
pf.edges.planChange: the plan check comes back not covered: self-pay, or a free cancel
pf.edges.twoBookings: a patient with a surgery and a check both open: Rosie asks which one before any change
pf.edges.healthQuestion: a question about medicine, blood thinners or eating before a visit goes to the surgeon; Rosie gives no advice
pf.edges.careHome: the resident is out (at the hospital, or asleep): the nurse says so, and the visit moves with no fee
pf.edges.other: all other edge cases the generic way
pf.edges.urgent: no service is sent now and nobody is on call (S2-30, S2-31): a post-surgery problem gets the soonest same-day time, with the owner's OK; swelling with a fever, or trouble breathing or swallowing, gets the 911 words

notes: Start: the dentist (clinic), refitted Oct 27. Names: Sam Lee, an oral surgeon, owns Lee Home Surgery LLC (the master's main company: mobile oral surgery at care homes and schools, 75 Mill Rd) and Lee Oral Surgery LLC (the second company: the office, 520 Harbor Ave). Flow A is at the office; flow B at Riverside care home, 64 Linden Rd, where Alex lives. Staff: Ruth (surgeon) and Marco (assistant) at the office; Jonah (surgeon) and Lucy (assistant) on the mobile team. Prices keep the master's own numbers: consult $35, fee $20, tooth removal $140 ($40 deposit, $100 rest), stitch removal $55 paid in full, night guard from photos $90 ($20 deposit, $70 rest), post-surgery check $25 ($110 in all), care-home check $179, care-home visit fee $89 ($245 in all), care-home extraction plan $640 ($160 deposit, $480 rest). Sedation and general anesthesia are never booked, priced or confirmed by Rosie: the office plans them by phone. Care-home visits are local numbing only. The $2 applies (D97): the 'No $2' branch of S1-62 is off. Licenses are optional and never checked (D96). Health work: sensitive on, so no rating is asked.
